#| echo: false

import glob
import json
import os
import platform
import socket
import subprocess
from datetime import datetime

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import networkx as nx
import pandas as pd
from IPython.display import Markdown, display

# A local build of this repository is used when present (or set DUCKDB / APT_EXTENSION), otherwise the
# community extension is installed into the duckdb found on the PATH
LOCAL_BUILD = "../build/release/extension/apt/apt.duckdb_extension"
APT_EXTENSION = os.environ.get("APT_EXTENSION", LOCAL_BUILD if os.path.exists(LOCAL_BUILD) else "")
DUCKDB = os.environ.get("DUCKDB", "../build/release/duckdb" if APT_EXTENSION == LOCAL_BUILD else "duckdb")
LOAD_APT = f"LOAD '{APT_EXTENSION}';" if APT_EXTENSION else "INSTALL apt FROM community; LOAD apt;"
# Audit another system (mounted disk image, container filesystem) instead of this machine
APT_ROOT = os.environ.get("APT_ROOT", "").rstrip("/")
ROOT = f"root := '{APT_ROOT}'" if APT_ROOT else ""
HOST = socket.gethostname() if not APT_ROOT else f"\\nolinkurl{{{os.path.normpath(APT_ROOT)}}} (offline audit)"


def query_apt(sql):
    # AI_AGENT switches the DuckDB CLI to its agent output mode, which is not JSON
    env = {key: value for key, value in os.environ.items() if key != "AI_AGENT"}
    result = subprocess.run(
        [DUCKDB, "-unsigned", "-json", ":memory:", "-c", f"{LOAD_APT} {sql}"],
        capture_output=True, text=True, env=env,
    )
    if result.returncode != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Query failed: {result.stderr}\n{sql}")
    output = result.stdout.strip()
    return pd.DataFrame(json.loads(output)) if output else pd.DataFrame()


# The report reads the database built by apt_database.sql: the same tables and views can be queried, shared or
# archived next to the PDF
DATABASE = os.environ.get("APT_DATABASE", "apt-security-report.duckdb")


def build_database():
    env = {key: value for key, value in os.environ.items() if key != "AI_AGENT"}
    command = [DUCKDB, "-unsigned", DATABASE, "-cmd", LOAD_APT]
    if APT_ROOT:
        command += ["-cmd", f"SET VARIABLE apt_root = '{APT_ROOT}'"]
    result = subprocess.run(command + ["-c", ".read apt_database.sql"], capture_output=True, text=True, env=env)
    if result.returncode != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Could not build {DATABASE}: {result.stderr}")


def query_db(sql):
    env = {key: value for key, value in os.environ.items() if key != "AI_AGENT"}

    def run(statement):
        result = subprocess.run([DUCKDB, "-readonly", "-json", DATABASE, "-c", statement],
                                capture_output=True, text=True, env=env)
        if result.returncode != 0:
            raise RuntimeError(f"Query failed: {result.stderr}\n{statement}")
        output = result.stdout.strip()
        return json.loads(output) if output else []

    rows = run(sql)
    if rows:
        return pd.DataFrame(rows)
    # JSON carries no column names for an empty result: get them from DESCRIBE
    return pd.DataFrame(columns=[column["column_name"] for column in run(f"DESCRIBE {sql}")])


def show(df, empty="*None.*"):
    display(Markdown(df.to_markdown(index=False) if len(df) else empty))


# Chart style: one hue for single-series charts, recessive axes, text in ink colors
BLUE = "#2a78d6"
NEUTRAL = "#b7b6b1"
INK = "#0b0b0b"
MUTED = "#52514e"
SEVERITY_COLORS = {"Critical": "#d03b3b", "High": "#ec835a", "Medium": "#fab219", "Low": "#9b9a95"}
SEVERITY_ICONS = {"Critical": "times-circle", "High": "exclamation-circle", "Medium": "exclamation-triangle", "Low": "info-circle"}
SEVERITY_ORDER = list(SEVERITY_COLORS)

plt.rcParams.update({
    "font.size": 10,
    "axes.edgecolor": NEUTRAL,
    "axes.labelcolor": MUTED,
    "axes.titlecolor": INK,
    "axes.titleweight": "bold",
    "axes.titlesize": 12,
    "axes.spines.top": False,
    "axes.spines.right": False,
    "xtick.color": MUTED,
    "ytick.color": INK,
})


def hbar(labels, values, title, xlabel, colors=BLUE, fmt="{:,.0f}", height=None):
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, height or max(2.5, 0.35 * len(labels) + 1)))
    ax.barh(labels, values, color=colors, height=0.6)
    ax.invert_yaxis()
    ax.grid(axis="x", color="#e4e3df", linewidth=0.8)
    ax.set_axisbelow(True)
    ax.spines["left"].set_visible(False)
    ax.tick_params(axis="y", length=0)
    for i, value in enumerate(values):
        ax.text(value, i, " " + fmt.format(value), va="center", color=INK, fontsize=9)
    ax.set_xlim(0, max(values) * 1.15 if len(values) else 1)
    ax.set_title(title, loc="left", pad=12)
    ax.set_xlabel(xlabel)
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()


def print_table(df, widths):
    # Pandoc sizes pipe-table columns by their share of dashes in the separator line, once a line is wider than 72
    # characters: the dashes below always are, so the widths are under control and long cells wrap within them
    # Identifiers such as "ubuntu-esm-infra.sources" must not be split at their hyphens
    print("```{=latex}\n\\begingroup\\footnotesize\\renewcommand{\\arraystretch}{1.4}"
          "\\hyphenpenalty=10000\\exhyphenpenalty=10000\n```\n")
    print("| " + " | ".join(df.columns) + " |")
    print("|" + "|".join("-" * width for width in widths) + "|")
    for row in df.itertuples(index=False):
        print("| " + " | ".join(str(value) for value in row) + " |")
    print("\n```{=latex}\n\\endgroup\n```\n")


def repository_uri(uri):
    # The scheme is dropped, plain HTTP is flagged by an open lock; \nolinkurl breaks long URIs at "/" and "."
    insecure = " \\textcolor{sevhigh}{\\faIcon{lock-open}}" if uri.startswith("http://") else ""
    return f"\\nolinkurl{{{uri.split('://', 1)[-1].rstrip('/')}}}{insecure}"


def severity(level):
    color = "sev" + level.lower()
    return f"\\textcolor{{{color}}}{{\\faIcon{{{SEVERITY_ICONS[level]}}}}} {level}"
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: false

# Data shared by all sections, from the tables and views of the database
build_database()
packages = query_db("SELECT * FROM packages")
if packages.empty:
    raise RuntimeError("No installed package found: is this a Debian-based system (or is APT_ROOT correct)?")
posture = query_db("SELECT * FROM security_posture").iloc[0]

sources = query_db("""
    SELECT regexp_extract(file, '[^/]+$') AS file, enabled, type, uri, suite, components, signed_by, trusted
    FROM sources
    ORDER BY file, suite, type
""")
enabled_sources = sources[sources["enabled"]] if len(sources) else sources

orphans = query_db("""
    SELECT name, version, regexp_replace(maintainer, '\\s*<.*>', '') AS vendor,
           round(installed_size_kb / 1024.0, 1) AS size_mb
    FROM orphaned_packages
    ORDER BY size_mb DESC
""")

not_in_repo = query_db("""
    SELECT name, installed_version, array_to_string(available_versions, ', ') AS available_versions
    FROM packages_not_in_repositories
    ORDER BY name
""")

repositories = query_db("""
    SELECT coalesce(r.label, r.origin, r.site) AS repository, coalesce(r.suite, '') AS suite,
           coalesce(r.component, '') AS component, u.installed_packages_published AS packages
    FROM repository_usage u
    JOIN repositories r USING (repository_id)
    WHERE u.installed_packages_published > 0
    ORDER BY packages DESC
""")

universe = query_db("""
    SELECT count(DISTINCT o.name) AS packages
    FROM package_origins o
    JOIN repositories r USING (repository_id)
    WHERE o.is_installed_version AND r.origin = 'Ubuntu' AND r.component = 'universe'
""")["packages"][0]
esm_apps = bool(len(enabled_sources)) and enabled_sources["uri"].str.contains("esm.ubuntu.com/apps").any()

upgradable = query_db("""
    SELECT u.*, p.held
    FROM upgrades u
    JOIN packages p USING (name, architecture)
    ORDER BY name
""")
if upgradable.empty:
    upgradable = pd.DataFrame(columns=["name", "architecture", "current_version", "new_version", "repository",
                                       "is_security", "held"])
security_upgrades = query_db("SELECT * FROM security_updates ORDER BY name")
held = packages[packages["held"]]
held_with_updates = query_db("SELECT * FROM held_packages WHERE missed_version IS NOT NULL")

apt_repositories = query_db("SELECT * FROM repositories ORDER BY site, suite")
# Indexes past their Valid-Until date: apt refuses to refresh them, so the system is stuck with old metadata
# (a broken or frozen mirror, or an attacker replaying old metadata to hide updates)
expired = query_db("SELECT site, suite, valid_until FROM expired_repositories ORDER BY valid_until")

history = query_db("SELECT * FROM history ORDER BY start_time")
recent = query_db("SELECT * FROM recent_changes ORDER BY start_time")
for frame in (history, recent):
    if len(frame):
        frame["start_time"] = pd.to_datetime(frame["start_time"])
failed = query_db("""
    SELECT *
    FROM failed_transactions
    WHERE start_time >= (SELECT max(start_time) FROM history) - INTERVAL 30 DAY
    ORDER BY start_time
""")

third_party = query_db("""
    SELECT name, version, regexp_replace(maintainer, '\\s*<.*>', '') AS vendor
    FROM third_party_packages
    ORDER BY name
""")

release_files = glob.glob(f"{APT_ROOT}/var/lib/apt/lists/*Release")
last_update = datetime.fromtimestamp(max(os.path.getmtime(f) for f in release_files)) if release_files else None
days_since_update = (datetime.now() - last_update).days if last_update else None


# Findings: (severity, finding, count, recommendation)
trusted_sources = enabled_sources[enabled_sources["trusted"]] if len(sources) else sources
unpinned_sources = enabled_sources[enabled_sources["signed_by"].isna()] if len(sources) else sources
http_sources = enabled_sources[enabled_sources["uri"].str.startswith("http://")] if len(sources) else sources
disabled_sources = sources[~sources["enabled"]] if len(sources) else sources
other_upgrades = len(upgradable) - len(security_upgrades)

findings = []
if len(trusted_sources):
    findings.append(("Critical", "Repositories with signature checks disabled (trusted=yes)", len(trusted_sources),
                     "Remove trusted=yes and pin the repository key with signed-by"))
if len(orphans):
    findings.append(("High", "Packages no configured repository provides: apt never updates them", len(orphans),
                     "Re-enable or add the vendor repository, switch to a maintained channel, or uninstall"))
if len(security_upgrades):
    findings.append(("High", "Security updates pending", len(security_upgrades),
                     "Apply them (apt upgrade) and check that unattended-upgrades is active"))
if len(held_with_updates):
    findings.append(("High", "Held packages (apt-mark hold) missing available updates", len(held_with_updates),
                     "Review why each package is held, and release the hold for security fixes"))
if len(expired):
    findings.append(("High", "Repository indexes past their Valid-Until date", len(expired),
                     "Run apt update and fix the mirror: expired metadata can hide security updates"))
if days_since_update is not None and days_since_update > 7:
    findings.append(("High", f"Package lists not refreshed for {days_since_update} days", 1,
                     "Run apt update regularly: every other finding depends on fresh lists"))
if len(unpinned_sources):
    findings.append(("Medium", "Repositories accepting any key of the global keyring (no signed-by)", len(unpinned_sources),
                     "Add signed-by= pointing to the vendor key only"))
if len(not_in_repo):
    findings.append(("Medium", "Installed versions that no repository provides", len(not_in_repo),
                     "Reinstall the repository version or document the local build"))
if other_upgrades > 0:
    findings.append(("Low", "Non-security updates pending", other_upgrades, "Apply during the next maintenance window"))
if len(http_sources):
    findings.append(("Low", "Repositories fetched over plain HTTP", len(http_sources),
                     "Signatures protect integrity, but HTTP exposes the software inventory: prefer HTTPS mirrors"))
if len(disabled_sources):
    findings.append(("Low", "Disabled repositories (their packages no longer get updates)", len(disabled_sources),
                     "Remove them, or re-enable them if their packages are still installed"))
if len(held) > len(held_with_updates):
    findings.append(("Low", "Held packages (apt-mark hold)", len(held) - len(held_with_updates),
                     "Document why they are held: they will silently miss future updates"))
if len(failed):
    findings.append(("Low", "Failed apt transactions in the last 30 days of history", len(failed),
                     "Check that the packages involved are in a consistent state (dpkg --audit)"))
if universe and not esm_apps:
    findings.append(("Low", "Packages from Ubuntu universe (community maintained)", int(universe),
                     "Enable Ubuntu Pro ESM Apps for security coverage of universe"))

findings = pd.DataFrame(findings, columns=["Severity", "Finding", "Count", "Recommendation"])
findings["rank"] = findings["Severity"].map(SEVERITY_ORDER.index)
findings = findings.sort_values(["rank", "Count"], ascending=[True, False]).drop(columns="rank")
```

        "Finding": [f"{f} (**{c}**)" for f, c in zip(findings["Finding"], findings["Count"])],
        "Recommendation": findings["Recommendation"],
    })
    print(table.to_markdown(index=False))
    print()

# \faIcon{info-circle} Scope and Method

The **apt** extension for DuckDB exposes the state of the apt/dpkg package manager as SQL tables. This report only reads local files, it does not modify the system or contact any server:

- **Installed packages**, from `/var/lib/dpkg/status` and `/var/lib/apt/extended_states`: `apt_packages()`, `apt_dependencies()`, `apt_provides()`
- **Configured repositories**, from `/etc/apt/sources.list` and `/etc/apt/sources.list.d/`: `apt_sources()`
- **Repositories, package origins and pending updates**, from the indexes downloaded by `apt update` in `/var/lib/apt/lists/`: `apt_repositories()`, `apt_package_origins()`, `apt_upgradable()`
- **Change history**, from `/var/log/apt/history.log` and its rotated files: `apt_history()`

Repositories, origins and pending updates are only as fresh as the last `apt update`. Software installed outside apt (snaps, Flatpaks, language package managers, manual installs in `/opt`) is **out of scope**.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

version = query_db("SELECT apt_version FROM snapshot")["apt_version"][0]
facts = pd.DataFrame([
    ("Host", HOST),
    ("Operating system", system),
    ("Kernel", platform.release() if not APT_ROOT else "n/a"),
    ("apt version", version or "n/a"),
    ("Report date", f"{datetime.now():%Y-%m-%d %H:%M}"),
], columns=["Item", "Value"])
print(facts.to_markdown(index=False))
```

# \faIcon{rocket} Getting Started with the apt Extension

## \faIcon{tachometer-alt} What the Extension Gives You

Each function replaces a command, or a parsing script, with a table that can be filtered, joined and exported. Rows and timings below are measured on this machine (timings include starting DuckDB):

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

import time

functions = [
    ("apt_packages()", "What is installed, how big, installed on purpose or as a dependency?",
     "`dpkg-query`, `apt-mark showauto`"),
    ("apt_dependencies()", "What depends on what?", "`apt-cache depends`, `apt-cache rdepends`"),
    ("apt_provides()", "Which package provides a virtual package?", "`apt-cache showpkg`"),
    ("apt_sources()", "Which repositories are configured, and how are they trusted?",
     "reading `sources.list.d` by hand"),
    ("apt_repositories()", "Which repositories were downloaded, and how fresh are they?",
     "`apt-cache policy`, reading Release files"),
    ("apt_package_origins()", "Which repository does each package come from?", "`apt-cache policy`, per package"),
    ("apt_upgradable()", "Which updates are pending, and which are security fixes?", "`apt list --upgradable`"),
    ("apt_history()", "Who installed, upgraded or removed what, and when?", "`zgrep` in `/var/log/apt`"),
]
rows = []
for function, question, replaces in functions:
    call = function.replace("()", f"({ROOT})")
    start = time.perf_counter()
    count = query_apt(f"SELECT count(*) AS n FROM {call}")["n"][0]
    elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start
    rows.append((f"\\texttt{{{function.replace('_', chr(92) + '_')}}}", question, replaces, f"{count:,}", f"{elapsed:.2f} s"))

print_table(pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["Function", "Answers", "Replaces", "Rows here", "Time"]),
            widths=[24, 34, 22, 10, 10])
index_mb = sum(os.path.getsize(f) for f in glob.glob(f"{APT_ROOT}/var/lib/apt/lists/*_Packages*")) / 1024 / 1024
print(f"`apt_package_origins()` cross-checks every installed package against **{index_mb:,.1f} MB** of repository "
      "indexes in a single query, where `apt-cache policy` answers for one package at a time.\n")
print("`apt_version_compare(a, b)` compares Debian versions exactly like `dpkg --compare-versions`, and every "
      "function reads files through DuckDB, so `SET enable_external_access = false` and `allowed_directories` "
      "restrict it like any other file access.\n")
```

## \faIcon{play} First Steps

The extension is distributed through the [DuckDB community extensions repository](https://duckdb.org/community_extensions/extensions/apt): from any DuckDB client (CLI, Python, R, ...), install it once and load it in each session:

```sql
INSTALL apt FROM community;
LOAD apt;

-- What did I install on purpose?
SELECT name, version
FROM apt_packages()
WHERE NOT auto_installed
ORDER BY name;

-- Which packages will apt never update?
SELECT name, version
FROM apt_packages()
ANTI JOIN apt_package_origins()
    USING (name, architecture);

-- Keep a snapshot, to compare machines
-- or track drift over time
COPY (SELECT * FROM apt_packages())
TO 'inventory.parquet';
```

Every table function except `apt_upgradable()` takes an optional `root` argument to audit another system, e.g. `apt_packages(root := '/mnt/image')`.

```{python}
#| echo: false

by_section = (packages.assign(section=packages["section"].fillna("(none)"))
              .groupby("section")["installed_size_kb"].sum()
              .sort_values(ascending=False).head(12) / 1024)
hbar(by_section.index.tolist(), by_section.values.tolist(),
     "Installed size by section (top 12)", "Installed size (MB)")

# \faIcon{link} Software Supply Chain

## \faIcon{server} Configured Repositories

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

if len(sources):
    keys = (sources["signed_by"].str.replace(r".*/", "", regex=True)
            .str.replace(r"(-keyring)?\.(gpg|asc)$", "", regex=True)
            .str.strip("()").fillna("\\textcolor{sevhigh}{any trusted key}"))
    table = (sources.assign(key=keys)
             .groupby(["file", "enabled", "uri", "key"], sort=False)["suite"]
             .agg(lambda suites: ", ".join(dict.fromkeys(suites))).reset_index())
    files = table["file"] + table["enabled"].map({True: "", False: "\\newline\\textcolor{gray}{\\footnotesize disabled}"})
    print_table(pd.DataFrame({
        "Source file": files,
        "Repository": table["uri"].map(repository_uri),
        "Suites": table["suite"].str.replace(", ", "\\newline ", regex=False),
        "Signing key": table["key"],
    }), widths=[23, 35, 21, 21])
    print("\\textcolor{sevhigh}{\\faIcon{lock-open}} fetched over plain HTTP. \\textcolor{gray}{disabled}: "
          "ignored by apt, the packages installed from it no longer get updates.\n")
else:
    print("*No repository configured.*")
```

A repository is trusted through the key named by `signed-by`. Without it, apt accepts a signature from **any** key of the global keyring, so any vendor key installed there could sign packages for every such repository. `trusted=yes` disables signature checks altogether.

## \faIcon{exclamation-triangle} Repository Risks

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

if len(sources):
    risky = enabled_sources.assign(
        plain_http=enabled_sources["uri"].str.startswith("http://"),
        no_signed_by=enabled_sources["signed_by"].isna(),
    )
    risky = risky[risky["plain_http"] | risky["no_signed_by"] | risky["trusted"]]
    flags = risky.apply(lambda r: ", ".join(
        flag for flag, on in [("signature checks disabled", r["trusted"]), ("no signed-by", r["no_signed_by"]),
                              ("plain HTTP", r["plain_http"])] if on), axis=1)
    if len(risky):
        print_table(pd.DataFrame({"Source file": risky["file"], "Repository": risky["uri"].map(repository_uri),
                                  "Suite": risky["suite"], "Risk": flags}), widths=[20, 38, 20, 22])
    else:
        print("*None.*")
```

## \faIcon{unlink} Orphaned Packages

These installed packages are **unknown to every configured repository**: they were installed from a downloaded `.deb`, or their repository was removed or disabled. `apt upgrade` will never update them, so their vulnerabilities stay open until someone updates them by hand.

```

## \faIcon{clock} Repository Freshness

Repositories republish their index (the `Release` file) when their packages change, so an old date alone is not a problem: a repository with nothing new to publish keeps its index. What protects against a stale mirror, or an attacker replaying old metadata to hide updates, is the `Valid-Until` date that some repositories (such as Debian's security archive) put in their index: apt refuses an index past it. Repositories without one, like Ubuntu's, cannot be checked this way.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

if len(apt_repositories):
    now = pd.Timestamp.now(tz="UTC").tz_localize(None)
    fresh = apt_repositories.assign(date=pd.to_datetime(apt_repositories["date"]),
                                    valid_until=pd.to_datetime(apt_repositories["valid_until"]))
    fresh = fresh.sort_values("date")

    def validity(valid_until):
        if pd.isna(valid_until):
            return "\\textcolor{gray}{not set}"
        text = f"{valid_until:%Y-%m-%d}"
        return f"\\textcolor{{sevcritical}}{{{text} expired}}" if valid_until < now else text

    print_table(pd.DataFrame({
        "Repository": fresh["site"].map(lambda s: f"\\nolinkurl{{{s}}}"),
        "Suite": fresh["suite"].fillna(""),
        "Component": fresh["component"].fillna(""),
        "Published": fresh["date"].dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d").fillna("unknown"),
        "Valid until": fresh["valid_until"].map(validity),
        "Security": fresh["is_security"].map({True: "\\textcolor{sevok}{\\faIcon{shield-alt}} yes", False: ""}),
    }), widths=[31, 20, 12, 12, 15, 10])
else:
    print("*No repository index: apt update has never run.*")
```

# \faIcon{project-diagram} Dependency Risk

A package many others depend on is a high-value target: a vulnerability or a compromise in it reaches everything above it. Virtual dependencies (such as `mail-transport-agent`) are resolved to the installed packages that provide them.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: false

# Hard dependencies between installed packages, virtual packages resolved to their providers
edges = query_db("""
    SELECT DISTINCT package, depends_on AS dependency
    FROM dependency_edges
    WHERE relation IN ('Pre-Depends', 'Depends') AND package <> depends_on
""")
graph = nx.DiGraph()
graph.add_nodes_from(packages["name"])
graph.add_edges_from(edges[["package", "dependency"]].itertuples(index=False, name=None))
```

## \faIcon{bullseye} Most Depended-On Packages

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 8

dependents = pd.Series(dict(graph.in_degree())).sort_values(ascending=False).head(15)
dependents = dependents[dependents > 0]
hbar(dependents.index.tolist(), dependents.values.tolist(),
     "Packages with the most direct dependents (top 15)", "Installed packages depending on it directly")
```

## \faIcon{sitemap} Transitive Reach

Direct dependents understate the reach of low-level libraries. The number of packages that depend on a package **directly or transitively** is its blast radius if it is compromised.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 8

candidates = pd.Series(dict(graph.in_degree())).sort_values(ascending=False).head(40).index
reach = pd.Series({node: len(nx.ancestors(graph, node)) for node in candidates})
reach = reach.sort_values(ascending=False).head(15)
reach = reach[reach > 0]
hbar(reach.index.tolist(), reach.values.tolist(),
     "Packages with the largest blast radius (top 15)", "Installed packages depending on it, directly or transitively")
```

## \faIcon{share-alt} Dependency Network and Centrality

Graph data science ranks packages beyond simple counts:

- **PageRank** scores a package by how much of the system depends on it, weighting dependents by their own importance: the targets of choice for a supply chain attack.
- **Betweenness centrality** measures how often a package lies on the dependency paths between other packages: the bridges through which a compromise propagates.

The network shows the (up to 25) packages with the largest blast radius and the dependencies between them. Node size is the number of direct dependents, color the betweenness centrality.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 8.5

from matplotlib.colors import LinearSegmentedColormap

# Betweenness on a sample of 500 source nodes: exact values cost O(nodes x edges)
betweenness = nx.betweenness_centrality(graph, k=min(500, graph.number_of_nodes()), seed=42)
pagerank = nx.pagerank(graph)
blast = {node: len(nx.ancestors(graph, node)) for node in candidates}
core = sorted(blast, key=blast.get, reverse=True)[:25]
sub = graph.subgraph(core).copy()
sub.remove_nodes_from(list(nx.isolates(sub)))
in_degree = dict(graph.in_degree())
core = list(sub.nodes())

# Single-hue sequential scale, light to dark blue
blues = LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list("blues", ["#cfe0f7", "#2a78d6", "#0d3a75"])
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 8.5))
pos = nx.kamada_kawai_layout(sub.to_undirected())
nx.draw_networkx_edges(sub, pos, ax=ax, edge_color="#d6d5d0", width=0.7, arrowsize=8, node_size=600,
                       connectionstyle="arc3,rad=0.08")
sizes = [150 + 1600 * in_degree[node] / max(in_degree[n] for n in core) for node in sub.nodes()]
colors = [betweenness[node] for node in sub.nodes()]
nodes = nx.draw_networkx_nodes(sub, pos, ax=ax, node_size=sizes, node_color=colors, cmap=blues,
                               edgecolors="white", linewidths=2)
for node, (x, y) in pos.items():
    ax.annotate(node, (x, y), xytext=(0, 9 + 10 * in_degree[node] / max(in_degree[n] for n in core)),
                textcoords="offset points", ha="center", fontsize=8, color=INK,
                bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.15", fc="white", ec="none", alpha=0.8))
colorbar = plt.colorbar(nodes, ax=ax, fraction=0.035, pad=0.02)
colorbar.set_label("Betweenness centrality", color=MUTED)
colorbar.outline.set_visible(False)
ax.set_title(f"Core dependency network: the {len(core)} packages with the largest blast radius", loc="left", pad=12)
ax.axis("off")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

top = sorted(pagerank, key=pagerank.get, reverse=True)[:10]
print_table(pd.DataFrame({
    "Package": top,
    "Direct dependents": [f"{in_degree[n]:,}" for n in top],
    "Blast radius": [f"{len(nx.ancestors(graph, n)):,}" for n in top],
    "PageRank": [f"{pagerank[n]:.4f}" for n in top],
    "Betweenness": [f"{betweenness[n]:.4f}" for n in top],
}), widths=[28, 18, 18, 18, 18])

hidden = [n for n in top if in_degree[n] <= 2 and len(nx.ancestors(graph, n)) > 1000]
if hidden:
    print(f"`{hidden[0]}` has only {in_degree[hidden[0]]} direct dependent(s), yet the blast radius of the packages "
          "depending on it: a package is as critical as what depends on it, which direct counts miss and PageRank "
          "captures.\n")

bridges = sorted(betweenness, key=betweenness.get, reverse=True)[:5]
print(f"The top bridges by betweenness are {', '.join(f'`{n}`' for n in bridges)}: they are not the most depended-on "
      "packages, but many dependency chains go through them, so they deserve the same patching priority.\n")
```

## \faIcon{external-link-alt} What Third-Party Software Pulls In

Third-party and orphaned packages run on top of distribution libraries: these are updated by the distribution, but the software using them is not reviewed by it. The more a third-party package relies on, the more it is exposed to their vulnerabilities.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 8

vendors = sorted(set(third_party["name"]) | set(orphans["name"]))
pulled_in = pd.Series({name: len(nx.descendants(graph, name)) for name in vendors}).sort_values(ascending=False)
if len(pulled_in) and pulled_in.max() > 0:
    hbar(pulled_in.index.tolist(), pulled_in.values.tolist(),
         "Installed packages each third-party package relies on", "Dependencies, direct and transitive")
```

A distribution library used by several third-party packages is a single point of exposure for all of them. The graph links each third-party package (left) to the direct dependencies it shares with at least one other (right).

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 7

shared = pd.Series([dep for name in vendors for _, dep in graph.out_edges(name)]).value_counts()
shared = shared[shared > 1].head(14)
links = [(name, dep) for name in vendors for _, dep in graph.out_edges(name) if dep in shared.index]
if links:
    left = sorted({name for name, _ in links}, key=lambda n: -sum(1 for v, _ in links if v == n))
    right = shared.index.tolist()
    pos = {name: (0, -i * (len(right) - 1) / max(len(left) - 1, 1)) for i, name in enumerate(left)}
    pos.update({dep: (1, -i) for i, dep in enumerate(right)})
    bipartite = nx.Graph(links)

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 7))
    nx.draw_networkx_edges(bipartite, pos, ax=ax, edge_color="#c9c8c3", width=0.9)
    nx.draw_networkx_nodes(bipartite, pos, nodelist=left, ax=ax, node_color=BLUE, node_size=180,
                           edgecolors="white", linewidths=2, label="Third-party or orphaned package")
    nx.draw_networkx_nodes(bipartite, pos, nodelist=right, ax=ax, node_color=NEUTRAL, node_size=120,
                           edgecolors="white", linewidths=2, label="Shared dependency")
    for name in left:
        ax.text(pos[name][0] - 0.03, pos[name][1], name, ha="right", va="center", fontsize=9, color=INK)
    for dep in right:
        ax.text(pos[dep][0] + 0.03, pos[dep][1], f"{dep} ({shared[dep]})", ha="left", va="center", fontsize=9,
                color=INK)
    ax.set_xlim(-0.6, 1.6)
    ax.legend(loc="upper center", bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, 0), ncol=2, frameon=False, labelcolor=INK)
    ax.set_title("Dependencies shared by third-party packages (number of users)", loc="left", pad=12)
    ax.axis("off")
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
```

# \faIcon{book} Appendix

## \faIcon{redo} Reproducing This Report

The report installs the extension from the community repository into the `duckdb` CLI found on the `PATH`:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/adriens/duckdb-apt && cd duckdb-apt
task report

# Audit another system, e.g. a mounted disk image
APT_ROOT=/mnt/image task report
```

## \faIcon{table} The Database Behind This Report

Every figure of this report is read from a DuckDB database built by [docs/apt_database.sql](https://github.com/adriens/duckdb-apt/blob/main/docs/apt_database.sql), saved next to this PDF. It holds plain tables, so it can be opened without the extension, queried, shared or archived to compare snapshots over time:

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

objects = query_db("""
    SELECT 'table' AS kind, table_name AS name, comment, estimated_size AS rows FROM duckdb_tables()
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 'view', view_name, comment, NULL FROM duckdb_views() WHERE NOT internal
    ORDER BY kind, name
""")
print_table(pd.DataFrame({
    "Object": objects.apply(lambda r: f"\\texttt{{{r['name'].replace('_', chr(92) + '_')}}} ({r['kind']})", axis=1),
    "Description": objects["comment"].fillna(""),
}), widths=[38, 62])
```

```sql
-- Open it with any DuckDB client
FROM security_posture;
SELECT name, version, installed_from, available_update
FROM package_overview
WHERE security_update;
```

## \faIcon{database} Key Queries

The findings come from plain SQL on top of the extension:

```sql
INSTALL apt FROM community;
LOAD apt;

-- Orphaned packages: unknown to every
-- configured repository (ANTI JOIN keeps the
-- packages without a matching origin)
SELECT p.name, p.version, p.maintainer
FROM apt_packages() p
ANTI JOIN apt_package_origins() o
    USING (name, architecture);

-- Risky repository settings
SELECT
    file,
    uri,
    suite,
    signed_by IS NULL AS no_signed_by,
    trusted
FROM apt_sources()
WHERE enabled
  AND (
      uri LIKE 'http://%'
      OR signed_by IS NULL
      OR trusted
  );

-- Pending security updates
SELECT
    name,
    current_version,
    new_version,
    repository
FROM apt_upgradable()
WHERE is_security;

-- Inventory as package URLs, for
-- vulnerability scanners (OSV, Grype,
-- Dependency-Track)
COPY (
    SELECT purl FROM apt_packages()
) TO 'inventory-purls.csv';
```

More queries in [docs/examples.sql](https://github.com/adriens/duckdb-apt/blob/main/docs/examples.sql).
